claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in fusion plasma-facing structural materials are governed by helium-vacancy cluster formation and mobility.
The material under consideration is polycrystalline tungsten with a uniform grain-size distribution.
Helium-ion irradiation introduces helium-vacancy clusters into polycrystalline tungsten.
Helium-vacancy cluster formation and mobility reduce the Peierls stress in tungsten.
Helium-vacancy cluster formation and mobility increase dislocation glide in tungsten.
Reduced Peierls stress and increased dislocation glide enhance high-temperature plastic strain.
Reduced Peierls stress and increased dislocation glide enhance toughness.
Helium-irradiated polycrystalline tungsten will exhibit greater plastic strain than unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten.
Helium-irradiated polycrystalline tungsten will exhibit greater toughness than unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten.
The hypothesis is expected to hold from 1000 to 2000 K under low-flux helium-ion irradiation.
The hypothesis is expected to hold only for helium-ion fluences below 10^22 ions/m^2.
Grain size and crystallographic orientation may affect helium-vacancy cluster formation and mobility.
A comparison between irradiated and unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten can test the predicted irradiation response.
Decreases in both plastic strain and toughness after irradiation would falsify the predicted enhancement.
